name: Altitude + water

chart.yLabel: body water after 4 h (% of normal)

overlay.caption: thin air → breathe harder · dry air + sweat → water out faster than it comes in

does: Shows less oxygen in each breath higher up, and faster breathing to make up for it
Shows more water lost at altitude, from sweating and from breathing hard in dry air
Shows that drinking more fixes the water problem but not the oxygen problem
doesnt: Measure any real person — the numbers are illustrative teaching values
Include the days-long adjustment to altitude, food, or temperature
Model altitude sickness or anything dangerous
limits.text: This is a simplified learning model. Real people vary with age, fitness and health. The numbers are illustrative, not measurements of any real person.
limits.wellbeing: A headache, feeling sick or being very short of breath on a mountain is a reason to rest, drink water and tell an adult.

sources: CK-12 Life Science: respiratory system and homeostasis
NOAA / NASA: how air pressure changes with altitude (student pages)
